chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I do not see that a man should swear except by Allah. As for the man's saying, 'No, by your adversary!', it is from the speech of the people of Ignorance, and if the man were to swear by this and its like, he would have neglected swearing by Allah. As for the man's saying, 'Ya Hayah and Ya Hanah', that is merely for seeking the name, and I do not see any harm in it. And as for his saying, 'La amr Allah' and his saying, 'La hahu', that is indeed by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.لَابَ: A negation particle often used in oaths
key_terms.لَعَمْرُ اللَّهِ: An oath formula meaning 'By my life, by Allah'

ai.seo_question: What are the different types of oaths and their rulings in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) establishes the theological principle that all valid oaths ultimately refer to Allah, distinguishing between pre-Islamic idioms like 'La ba li shani'ika' which are discouraged to preserve monotheistic purity, and common phrases like 'La amr Allah' which are explicitly affirmed as oaths by Him. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on purifying linguistic practices from Jahiliyyah influences while maintaining practical flexibility in daily speech.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not see that the man should swear except by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So as for the words of the man, ‘No, by your adversary!’, so it is from the worlds of the people of the ignorance, and if the man were to swear by this, and the likes of it he would have neglected the swearing by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So as for the words of the man, ‘يَا هَيَاهْ وَ يَا هَنَاهْ’, but rather that is for seeking the name, and I<sup>asws</sup> do not see by it any evil; and as for his words, ‘لَعَمْرُ اللَّهِ’, and his words, ‘لَا هَاهُ’, so rather that is (swearing) by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

I say that a man must take an oath and swear by Allah only. People’s saying, la’ bal shane ’uka (no, but may your adversary be it) is of the expressions of the people of ignorance. If one takes an oath by such expressions and so on, he has ignored taking an oath by Allah. One’s expression, Ya Hayahu and ya Hanahu is only a pausing and punctuating effort to better articulate one’s idea. However, one’s saying la’umr Allah or Lahahu is swearing by Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
